_comment: THE CI TEST MATRIX, AND THE TWO FACTS THE PANEL CANNOT LEARN FROM A RELEASE. released_nodes is the set the compatibility matrix exercises — the planner slices it by POSITION at min_supported — so a version missing from it is a version nothing tests. wire and features are the protocol generation and the capabilities this panel requires of a node; features.agent_upgrade_v1.required_capabilities is the one gate the upgrade path still has, and TestNodeV4CompatibilityMatrixMatchesSharedProtocolPolicy pins it to the shared protocol package. IT NO LONGER DECIDES WHAT THE PANEL OFFERS. It used to be an allow-list, with per-release display metadata (review notes, install methods, platforms, a published Docker tag) that the panel fetched and the dialog rendered — so adding a release meant editing this file, pinning its commit and publishing a panel. The catalog now lists the releases this project has PUBLISHED and reads what each release says about itself, which is why those fields are gone from the rows: leaving them would be a second, unread copy of what the assets already state. The document also used to name docs/compat/releases-v1.json as the signed admission policy beside it; that policy has been deleted, and what an operator may install is their choice among the published releases.
min_supported_doc: The OLDEST Passwall-Node version this panel still tests. Everything from this row onward in released_nodes is the supported set, and that set is exactly what the released-range CI matrix exercises. MATCHED BY POSITION IN released_nodes, NOT by a version comparison. The positional rule was introduced because the legacy scheme's dotless prereleases sorted wrongly as text ('v0.0.1-beta9' above 'v0.0.1-beta11'), so comparing the strings would have silently inverted the floor. THAT REASON IS GONE - a version is three integers now, and integers compare correctly - and the mechanism stays because it is the one both sides already implement: the planner slices this list by indexOf exactly as this field is read. THIS SELECTS WHAT IS TESTED, NOT WHAT MAY CONNECT. No production code reads this field -- only the two workflows and the matrix test do -- so raising it stops testing the versions below it and does nothing else: an older node keeps syncing, and nothing refuses it for sitting below this row. Refusing a node is a separate decision about the wire generation (see wire.min_protocol_version) and needs its own change, announcement and migration acceptance; a floor move must not do that work by implication. Raising it is still BREAKING in the sense that matters here: every version below it stops being tested, so a regression in one of them stops being caught. Record it in docs/compat-policy.md's history, naming what is now untested. The field exists so the matrix can stop growing -- without a floor every release adds a permanent row.
